title: Fortresses and Defensive Draws
description: Sometimes a material deficit can be held with a fortress — an impregnable setup the stronger side cannot break. Learn to build defensive walls and save lost-looking endings.

sections.title: The Idea of a Fortress
sections.content: A fortress is a position where the defending side, though materially worse, sets up a wall the opponent simply cannot break. Recognizing fortress potential can save half points from seemingly lost positions.

positions.commentary: A lone bishop cannot deliver mate, and many bishop endings without pawns are dead draws. Knowing which material cannot win is a vital defensive skill.

sections.title: Building the Wall
sections.content: Defensive fortresses often rely on a blockade — placing pieces and pawns so the enemy king and pieces have no entry. Keep the structure intact and avoid creating new weaknesses.

positions.commentary: Locked pawns and opposing kings can produce a fortress where neither side can break through, ending in a draw despite the tension.

exercises.title: Hold the Wall
exercises.description: White to play. Maintain the blockade and opposition to hold the draw.
hints: Do not let the black king in
